comments.author: @WhoWouldWantThisName
comments.text:
I think humans always want to boil everything down into some overly simple narrative like it's a hollyweird movie. The reality is there's a ton of different reasons for the variety of changes that have gone on for decades and while I'm not gullible and have been I suppose "aware", "red pilled", etc. for about 35 years now I can still see how's and why's to explain most things that don't have a globalist NWO origin. That said, that is also a very real thing in itself. Could it be that entire industries are manipulated to shift in a particular direction? Absolutely, and that is also real. That does not mean, however, that they are somehow all "in on it" either. They do what they have to to survive as well and to prosper if possible.

This also applies to govt.. If you think somehow ALL, or even most, of "them" are in on some conspiracy of tyranny that is also not being wise or shrewd. That is being ridiculous. You can't get everyone in any organization on board with anything, let alone get them to keep it all a secret. Most veterans have learned that from their experience with govt. from that perspective. The only thing simple about any of this is that there are few decisions in life that are made that are clear and simple. Most come with a compromise of good and bad. So for every time someone complains about the jobs going away to another country there's someone else griping about not being able to buy a far cheaper foreign competitor's product. Well, would you rather pay more for an American one that supports Americans working there, or pay less but have fewer employed people here at home? It's one or the other. They want more decent paying jobs, like in construction, yet they don't want the bldgs. they are building or the infrastructure needed to support that. You can't have it both ways. People complained about the pollution and deforestation, etc., so paper products went away and so did the logging industry. Then those people went to other jobs that got ended over some other reason that the people didn't want that either. They didn't want those factories polluting the air, so those jobs went oversees and the ex-employees remained here unemployed. Some used to be loggers and now they are ex auto workers. This goes on and on and the same people gripe about "no good jobs", "no good paying jobs", "why's everything so expensive?", "why's everything affordable made in China?", and so on.

Lastly, and this is a bigger one than get's addressed, so many people now work remotely which means they can work anywhere and live anywhere else. This means they make big expensive city wages/salaries yet move to cheap places to live. They pay whatever it costs for the lavish lifestyle they want, and can now afford in their new home town. This creates a new economy there catering to that customer base. All prices adjust upwards and it's no longer a cheap place to live. If you want to know why you still make the pay you did 5 years ago when a house there was $150k but that house now costs $500k, well there you go. We used to have local economies that were self regulating by not being ran by outside influence. Now we live in a global, or at least national economy where people's spending habits across the county impact the price of the goods you buy. Most of this goes back to the internet and all that connection made possible with it. I don't think I'd want to be without it but a lot of trouble has come with it as the cost.
